text:
Adele: Heads-up — after the 6.5 kernel rollout to eu-west2 last night we're seeing a cluster-wide spike in GPU host reboots and pod evictions. not just p4s, a few a10s too.
Ravi: saw that, noticed nv-host reset and 'gpu device lost' in dmesg on a handful of hosts. kicking off a triage runbook.
Noah: logs show repeated: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:07:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" then later modprobe unload errors.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: kernel-6.5 rollout completed for region eu-west2 at 2026-03-17T23:40:12Z.
Sam: NCCL errors in training jobs too — handshake timeouts and transient peer disconnects. likely PCI link flaps.
Marina: capacity alarms: autoscaler is provisioning extra nodes but they fail node-problem-detector checks and end up NotReady -> provisioning churn and cost spike.
Adele: mitigation proposals: 1) pause further 6.5 rollouts, 2) force rollback to 5.15 AMI for critical pools, 3) push driver 535.86.05 build with patched module-symversions, or 4) temporarily cordon GPU node pools and route jobs to Dedicated until we patch.
Noah: quick check — driver 535 branch has a known fix for nvlink reset under k6.5 in internal patches, but we need a test build. building now on ci-gpu-1.
Ravi: we should also consider adding a udev rule to wait for /dev/nvidia* creation before kubelet registers the node as Ready to avoid immediate crash loop on attach. cheap stopgap.
Marina: customers on Dedicated asking whether their workloads are affected — status page already updated but we need an internal communications plan for enterprise tenants.
Adele: ops: start controlled rollback for autoscaled pools in eu-west2 AZ-a and AZ-b only. keep one AZ on 6.5 as a canary.
Ravi: rolling back will reduce our short-term cost surge but we need to drain workloads gracefully (preStop 30s) to avoid failed jobs; I'm starting a drain script now.
Noah: note — I saw at least 3 hosts with 'NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus' followed by 'kernel panic - not syncing' on a custom AMI. those need immediate evacuation.
InfraBot: alert: host eu-west2-p4-004 marked unschedulable by node-problem-detector at 1890123489.
Sam: For longer term: add kernel-compat tests to CI matrix that boot nodes with driver permutations (528/535/540) and run a mini NCCL ring to detect flapping. This would've caught the regression.
Marina: Ops asks to estimate rollback impact on SLAs and ticketing load. Product and Customer Success on standby.
Adele: I've opened an incident in incidents with draft postmortem template. tagging oncall and eng-sre.
Ravi: for immediate hotfix, I'll attempt to rebuild DKMS packages with signed module support and push via apt mirror, then trigger a rolling package update on non-canary AZ. if that fails, rollback.
Noah: keep an eye on PCIe AER logs — if we see correctable error rates rise, that points to hardware/firmware interplay with the new kernel. file bug with vendor if needed.
Sam: tracking checklist: 1) pause rollout (done?), 2) start rollback (Adele), 3) build+test driver patch (Noah), 4) udev gating (Ravi), 5) customer comms (Marina).
Adele: pause request sent to rollout service, confirmed paused. starting rollback to 5.15 for gpu-pool-eu-west2-1 now. ETA 45m for steps to finish and health checks.
Marina: posting to status.redwood.ai: "We are investigating GPU host instability in eu-west2 following a kernel upgrade. Some workloads may see restarts or provisioning delays. Investigating fixes and rollbacks."
OpsBot: reaction :thumbsup: to Adele
Noah: after we stabilize, let's add a post-upgrade smoke test that runs a quick cudaMemTest + NCCL ring across one host per AZ. saves us from these noisy incidents.
Adele: agreed. once rollback completes, schedule retrospective and prioritize CI tests and signed module packaging in the infra backlog.
Marina: I'll coordinate customer comms and send a note to enterprise contacts.
Ravi: continuing DKMS build. I'll post updates here.
Noah: update 1890123500 — initial driver build succeeded locally, planning small rolling canary tomorrow 07:00 UTC.
Adele: thanks everyone — keep updates short here. if you need to escalate, ping me directly.
Noah: logs show repeated: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:07:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" then later modprobe unload errors.
Adele: exact dmesg snippet pasted to thread:
Noah: ````
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:07:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568112] nvlink: link 1 reset detected, peer lost
[ 1234.569000] nvidia: Probe of device failed, dropping driver
[ 1234.569210] modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in /lib/modules/6.5.0-rc
````
Ravi: interesting — modprobe failure indicates DKMS didn't build for this kernel variant (we pushed a vanilla 6.5 image). some hosts show the module present but symbol version mismatches.
Sam: if DKMS fails, kubelet will still try to schedule gpu workloads and they'll OOM or crash quickly -> eviction storms.
